## Report: staff workspace gateway for workspace.trynxeon.com **Nothing was applied** to production, nginx, DNS, Cloudflare, a node or a VM. Branch `feature/workspace-gateway`, one commit `32434ef9f9`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-workspace` (real `node_modules` copy, no symlinks, `/opt/nxeon` untouched). Notes are in `/root/agent-notes/workspace.md`. Hostname follows the owner's change: nothing assumes nxeon.cloud for the workspace. ### Decisions you should know about - **Cookie.** The main session cookie `nxeon_session` is host-only and is not widened. A test fails if `lib/auth.ts` ever gains a `domain` attribute. - **Login hop.** The workspace is on a different registrable domain, so nginx there can never see that cookie. The flow is `workspace.trynxeon.com/_nx/start` → `nxeon.cloud/api/workspace/login` → a signed 60-second, single-use grant → `/_nx/callback` → host-only `__Host-nxws` cookie (8h, Lax so the cross-site redirect carries it). - The nonce cookie blocks login-CSRF. - Redirects use a fixed origin plus a sanitised path. - Logout is `POST /_nx/logout`. - **Who passes.** `GET /api/workspace/auth` returns 200 only when all of these hold: - the gateway cookie is valid and unexpired; - the user exists, is not suspended, and has the same `sessionVersion`; - the originating session is not revoked; - the role is `SUPPORT`, `BILLING` or `ADMIN`. `EMPLOYEE` is admitted only via `WORKSPACE_ROLES`; `CUSTOMER` never is; - 2FA is present if `enforce_staff_2fa` or `WORKSPACE_REQUIRE_2FA=1` demands it. - The check re-runs against the DB on every request, so revocation is immediate. Impersonated sessions are refused at the hop. `allowed_admin_ips` is honoured at the hop. Any error fails closed. - **Identity headers.** nginx sets `X-Nxeon-User`, `-Email`, `-Role`, `-Ts` and `-Sig` and overwrites client copies. `-Sig` is an HMAC with a new `WORKSPACE_UPSTREAM_SECRET`, which the starter app verifies and fails closed on. It is the real protection because nginx can't strip header wildcards, and other VMs on node-4's private network could reach the port otherwise. - **Cloudflare token (finding).** `CLOUDFLARE_DNS_API_TOKEN` is valid but sees only the nxeon.cloud zone, not trynxeon.com. I confirmed this with a read-only lookup and created nothing. The DNS script needs a token you create, scoped to trynxeon.com with Zone:Read and DNS:Edit. Passed as `CF_TRYNXEON_TOKEN`, it is never stored. You can also add the record by hand (runbook step 5). - **Proxied vs DNS-only.** - **Mode:** create the record DNS-only first, then flip to proxied (orange cloud) as the steady state. - **Why proxied:** DDoS/WAF in front of a service exposing terminals, and it matches the apex. - **Origin lock:** while proxied, the workspace vhost on 443 accepts only Cloudflare IPs (anything else gets 444) and takes the real client IP from `CF-Connecting-IP`. The ranges are fetched at install time with sanity checks, and `--refresh-cf` updates them. Websockets work. - **Cost:** Cloudflare's ~100s idle timeout means the app must stream or send keepalive pings. - **Fallback:** `WS_PROXIED=0` re-renders for DNS-only. - **Certificate.** certbot webroot HTTP-01, as every other vhost uses (same ACME account, ecdsa). The installer issues it on first apply using a bootstrap HTTP-only vhost. Origin CA was rejected. - **VM-side rule.** The VM firewall allows the primary's public IP (51.79.162.96), not "the NAT gateway". The node DNATs without rewriting the source, so the VM sees the primary's IP. Verify with `ss` after the first request; the runbook explains how to swap to 10.20.3.1 if that is what you actually see. ### What the owner must run, in order (details in `docs/WORKSPACE-GATEWAY.md`) 1. Add `WORKSPACE_UPSTREAM_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)` to `/opt/nxeon/.env`. Optional extras: `WORKSPACE_ORIGIN`, `WORKSPACE_ROLES`, `WORKSPACE_REQUIRE_2FA`, `WORKSPACE_TTL_HOURS`. Then merge the branch and run `scripts/deploy-staging.sh `, check staging, then `scripts/promote-production.sh`. Smoke test: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Host: nxeon.cloud' http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/workspace/auth` should print 401. 2. In the admin UI, server `nxeon-team-pm` → add a tcp port forward to guest port 3000. Note the allocated public port **P**. If the VM isn't a `Server` row in the DB, stop; don't hand-edit `NXEON_FWD_N4`. 3. node-4 firewall: - On the primary run `scripts/workspace-node4-fw-check.sh` (offline `nft -c`, verified OK). - Diff node-4's `firewall.nft` against `scripts/firewall-node.nft`. - Splice `deploy/workspace-node4-forward.nft.snippet` into `chain forward` before the `iifname "vmbr1" accept` line. - Apply via `firewall-safe-apply.sh --check`, `--apply`, prove a new SSH connection works, then `--confirm`. - The snippet reuses `@nxeon_agent_allow_v4`; confirm node-4's `/etc/nxeon/agent-allow.nft` contains 51.79.162.96. 4. On the VM, snapshot VM 647, then follow `workspace-app-starter/README.md`: - create user `nxeon-ws`; - write `/etc/nxeon-workspace/env` with the same secret, `BIND_HOST=10.20.3.112` and `I_UNDERSTAND_GATEWAY_ONLY=1`; - install the systemd unit; - run `./vm-firewall.sh`, then `--apply`, plus `ufw allow 22/tcp` before `ufw enable`. 5. DNS: `cd /opt/nxeon && CF_TRYNXEON_TOKEN=… npx tsx scripts/workspace-dns-add.ts` is a dry run. Adding `--apply` creates only `workspace A 51.79.162.96`, DNS-only. It refuses if the host exists in any form and never touches MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC or the apex. 6. nginx on the primary, as root, with `export WS_UPSTREAM_PORT=

`: - `WS_PROXIED=0 scripts/workspace-gateway-install.sh --check` - `WS_PROXIED=0 scripts/workspace-gateway-install.sh --apply` (issues the cert, installs, runs `nginx -t`, reloads, post-checks) 7. Verify per runbook section 5. Then go proxied: `CF_TRYNXEON_TOKEN=… npx tsx scripts/workspace-dns-add.ts --set-proxied=true --apply`, then `scripts/workspace-gateway-install.sh --apply` (default `WS_PROXIED=1`). 8. Add Cloudflare Rules scoped to this hostname only, not zone-wide: cache bypass, SSL Full (strict), Rocket Loader / minify / email-obfuscation off. Set a monthly reminder for `--refresh-cf`. 9. Rollback: `scripts/workspace-gateway-install.sh --rollback`. Quick kill: remove the `sites-enabled` symlink, then `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`. The other layers' rollbacks (DNS, node-4 firewall, VM snapshot) are in runbook section 6. ### Files - **Auth:** `lib/workspace-gateway.ts` (pure core), `lib/workspace-gateway-server.ts`, `app/api/workspace/{auth,start,login,callback,logout}/route.ts` - **Tests:** `test/workspace-gateway.test.ts` - **nginx:** `deploy/workspace.trynxeon.com.nginx.conf`, `deploy/workspace-gateway.{http.conf.template,guard.snippet,hop.snippet}` - **Installer:** `scripts/workspace-gateway-install.sh` - **DNS:** `scripts/workspace-dns-add.ts` - **node-4 firewall:** `deploy/workspace-node4-forward.nft.snippet`, `scripts/workspace-node4-fw-check.sh` - **VM project:** `workspace-app-starter/` (`server.js`, `identity.js`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `ALLOWLIST.md`, `nxeon-workspace.service`, `vm-firewall.sh`, `.env.example`, `package.json`) - **Docs:** `docs/WORKSPACE-GATEWAY.md`, a new section in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` ### Verified - **Typecheck and tests.** `tsc --noEmit` is clean and the new 24 tests pass. They cover: - staff, support, billing, customer, employee, suspended and demoted users; - no-token, garbage, wrong-key, wrong-type, `alg=none` and expired tokens; - revocation, grant/state misuse and 2FA; - an open-redirect corpus; - header spoofing and signature checks, with the starter's verifier checked against the gateway's signer; - cookie-scope tripwires. - **nginx, on a private throwaway instance** (ports 18443/18080, `scripts/…/wsh` in the scratchpad) against a stand-in for the routes built on the real lib. The production nginx was never touched. - The full login hop works end to end. - An unauthenticated navigation gets a 302, a fetch gets 401, and forged headers or cookies get 401. - Client-spoofed `X-Nxeon-*` headers are overwritten. - The gateway cookie is stripped from the upstream `Cookie` header. - A websocket upgrade works when authed and gets 401 when not. - `/_nx_auth` and unknown `/_nx/*` return 404. - A non-Cloudflare peer gets 444. - A customer is denied (403). - The security headers are present. - The starter app refuses unsigned requests. - **Installer, with stubbed nginx/systemctl/curl/certbot in a temp dir.** It passed apply, idempotent re-apply (no reload), `--check`, failure-restore (local edit preserved, zero reloads) and rollback to the pre-existing state. Against the real box, `--check` correctly refuses because the app doesn't have the routes yet. - **Other checks.** `nft -c` parses node-4's firewall with the new rule spliced in. The DNS script's dry-run path and its missing-token and bad-token errors work. - **Cloudflare read-only check.** The platform token is active and sees only nxeon.cloud. Nothing was created or changed. ### Could not verify - Certificate issuance and renewal behind Cloudflare, and Cloudflare's own behaviour (524 timing, websocket idle, Set-Cookie and redirects through the proxy). - The node-4 rule's packet path and the real source IP seen inside the VM. The existing comment in `firewall-node.nft` says DNAT'd traffic never reaches that chain; I believe it does reach `forward`, and the `workspace-deny` counters in runbook step 3 will show which is right. - The VM ufw rules. - A real-browser run of the cross-site hop. The SameSite reasoning is from the rules, not a browser. - The Next route handlers under `next build` or `next start` (typechecked only), and the real DB paths and `/login?next=` round-trip. - Whether node-4's installed `firewall.nft` has diverged from the template. - Known limits: grant single-use tracking is in-process memory, as `claimOnce` is elsewhere, and the grant sits in a URL for up to 60 seconds. Both are documented. ### Process note Early on, a `pkill -f` pattern in my own test cleanup matched my own shell and killed it. It hit nothing else. I cleaned up the remaining test processes by PID, and recorded the lesson in the notes.

I confirmed this with a read-only lookup and created nothing. The DNS script needs a token you create, scoped to trynxeon.com with Zone:Read and DNS:Edit. Passed as `CF_TRYNXEON_TOKEN`, it is never stored. You can also add the record by hand (runbook step 5). - **Proxied vs DNS-only.** - **Mode:** create the record DNS-only first, then flip to proxied (orange cloud) as the steady state. - **Why proxied:** DDoS/WAF in front of a service exposing terminals, and it matches the apex. - **Origin lock:** while proxied, the workspace vhost on 443 accepts only Cloudflare IPs (anything else gets 444) and takes the real client IP from `CF-Connecting-IP`. The ranges are fetched at install time with sanity checks, and `--refresh-cf` updates them. Websockets work. - **Cost:** Cloudflare's ~100s idle timeout means the app must stream or send keepalive pings. - **Fallback:** `WS_PROXIED=0` re-renders for DNS-only. - **Certificate.** certbot webroot HTTP-01, as every other vhost uses (same ACME account, ecdsa). The installer issues it on first apply using a bootstrap HTTP-only vhost. Origin CA was rejected. - **VM-side rule.** The VM firewall allows the primary's public IP (51.79.162.96), not "the NAT gateway". The node DNATs without rewriting the source, so the VM sees the primary's IP. Verify with `ss` after the first request; the runbook explains how to swap to 10.20.3.1 if that is what you actually see. ### What the owner must run, in order (details in `docs/WORKSPACE-GATEWAY.md`) 1. Add `WORKSPACE_UPSTREAM_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)` to `/opt/nxeon/.env`. Optional extras: `WORKSPACE_ORIGIN`, `WORKSPACE_ROLES`, `WORKSPACE_REQUIRE_2FA`, `WORKSPACE_TTL_HOURS`. Then merge the branch and run `scripts/deploy-staging.sh `, check staging, then `scripts/promote-production.sh`. Smoke test: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Host: nxeon.cloud' http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/workspace/auth` should print 401. 2. In the admin UI, server `nxeon-team-pm` → add a tcp port forward to guest port 3000. Note the allocated public port **P**. If the VM isn't a `Server` row in the DB, stop; don't hand-edit `NXEON_FWD_N4`. 3. node-4 firewall: - On the primary run `scripts/workspace-node4-fw-check.sh` (offline `nft -c`, verified OK). - Diff node-4's `firewall.nft` against `scripts/firewall-node.nft`. - Splice `deploy/workspace-node4-forward.nft.snippet` into `chain forward` before the `iifname "vmbr1" accept` line. - Apply via `firewall-safe-apply.sh --check`, `--apply`, prove a new SSH connection works, then `--confirm`. - The snippet reuses `@nxeon_agent_allow_v4`; confirm node-4's `/etc/nxeon/agent-allow.nft` contains 51.79.162.96. 4. On the VM, snapshot VM 647, then follow `workspace-app-starter/README.md`: - create user `nxeon-ws`; - write `/etc/nxeon-workspace/env` with the same secret, `BIND_HOST=10.20.3.112` and `I_UNDERSTAND_GATEWAY_ONLY=1`; - install the systemd unit; - run `./vm-firewall.sh`, then `--apply`, plus `ufw allow 22/tcp` before `ufw enable`. 5. DNS: `cd /opt/nxeon && CF_TRYNXEON_TOKEN=… npx tsx scripts/workspace-dns-add.ts` is a dry run. Adding `--apply` creates only `workspace A 51.79.162.96`, DNS-only. It refuses if the host exists in any form and never touches MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC or the apex. 6. nginx on the primary, as root, with `export WS_UPSTREAM_PORT=

`: - `WS_PROXIED=0 scripts/workspace-gateway-install.sh --check` - `WS_PROXIED=0 scripts/workspace-gateway-install.sh --apply` (issues the cert, installs, runs `nginx -t`, reloads, post-checks) 7. Verify per runbook section 5. Then go proxied: `CF_TRYNXEON_TOKEN=… npx tsx scripts/workspace-dns-add.ts --set-proxied=true --apply`, then `scripts/workspace-gateway-install.sh --apply` (default `WS_PROXIED=1`). 8. Add Cloudflare Rules scoped to this hostname only, not zone-wide: cache bypass, SSL Full (strict), Rocket Loader / minify / email-obfuscation off. Set a monthly reminder for `--refresh-cf`. 9. Rollback: `scripts/workspace-gateway-install.sh --rollback`. Quick kill: remove the `sites-enabled` symlink, then `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`. The other layers' rollbacks (DNS, node-4 firewall, VM snapshot) are in runbook section 6. ### Files - **Auth:** `lib/workspace-gateway.ts` (pure core), `lib/workspace-gateway-server.ts`, `app/api/workspace/{auth,start,login,callback,logout}/route.ts` - **Tests:** `test/workspace-gateway.test.ts` - **nginx:** `deploy/workspace.trynxeon.com.nginx.conf`, `deploy/workspace-gateway.{http.conf.template,guard.snippet,hop.snippet}` - **Installer:** `scripts/workspace-gateway-install.sh` - **DNS:** `scripts/workspace-dns-add.ts` - **node-4 firewall:** `deploy/workspace-node4-forward.nft.snippet`, `scripts/workspace-node4-fw-check.sh` - **VM project:** `workspace-app-starter/` (`server.js`, `identity.js`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `ALLOWLIST.md`, `nxeon-workspace.service`, `vm-firewall.sh`, `.env.example`, `package.json`) - **Docs:** `docs/WORKSPACE-GATEWAY.md`, a new section in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` ### Verified - **Typecheck and tests.** `tsc --noEmit` is clean and the new 24 tests pass. They cover: - staff, support, billing, customer, employee, suspended and demoted users; - no-token, garbage, wrong-key, wrong-type, `alg=none` and expired tokens; - revocation, grant/state misuse and 2FA; - an open-redirect corpus; - header spoofing and signature checks, with the starter's verifier checked against the gateway's signer; - cookie-scope tripwires. - **nginx, on a private throwaway instance** (ports 18443/18080, `scripts/…/wsh` in the scratchpad) against a stand-in for the routes built on the real lib. The production nginx was never touched. - The full login hop works end to end. - An unauthenticated navigation gets a 302, a fetch gets 401, and forged headers or cookies get 401. - Client-spoofed `X-Nxeon-*` headers are overwritten. - The gateway cookie is stripped from the upstream `Cookie` header. - A websocket upgrade works when authed and gets 401 when not. - `/_nx_auth` and unknown `/_nx/*` return 404. - A non-Cloudflare peer gets 444. - A customer is denied (403). - The security headers are present. - The starter app refuses unsigned requests. - **Installer, with stubbed nginx/systemctl/curl/certbot in a temp dir.** It passed apply, idempotent re-apply (no reload), `--check`, failure-restore (local edit preserved, zero reloads) and rollback to the pre-existing state. Against the real box, `--check` correctly refuses because the app doesn't have the routes yet. - **Other checks.** `nft -c` parses node-4's firewall with the new rule spliced in. The DNS script's dry-run path and its missing-token and bad-token errors work. - **Cloudflare read-only check.** The platform token is active and sees only nxeon.cloud. Nothing was created or changed. ### Could not verify - Certificate issuance and renewal behind Cloudflare, and Cloudflare's own behaviour (524 timing, websocket idle, Set-Cookie and redirects through the proxy). - The node-4 rule's packet path and the real source IP seen inside the VM. The existing comment in `firewall-node.nft` says DNAT'd traffic never reaches that chain; I believe it does reach `forward`, and the `workspace-deny` counters in runbook step 3 will show which is right. - The VM ufw rules. - A real-browser run of the cross-site hop. The SameSite reasoning is from the rules, not a browser. - The Next route handlers under `next build` or `next start` (typechecked only), and the real DB paths and `/login?next=` round-trip. - Whether node-4's installed `firewall.nft` has diverged from the template. - Known limits: grant single-use tracking is in-process memory, as `claimOnce` is elsewhere, and the grant sits in a URL for up to 60 seconds. Both are documented. ### Process note Early on, a `pkill -f` pattern in my own test cleanup matched my own shell and killed it. It hit nothing else. I cleaned up the remaining test processes by PID, and recorded the lesson in the notes.

content.text:
I built the staff workspace gateway for workspace.trynxeon.com on branch `feature/workspace-gateway` (commit `32434ef9f9`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-workspace`). Nothing has been applied to production, nginx, DNS, Cloudflare, any node or any VM. The runbook is `docs/WORKSPACE-GATEWAY.md`, notes are in `/root/agent-notes/workspace.md`, and the full report went to the caller.

- **Cookie:** the main session cookie stays host-only and is not widened. Because workspace.trynxeon.com is a different registrable domain, a login hop issues a separate host-only gateway cookie. It goes nxeon.cloud → a signed 60-second single-use grant → workspace.trynxeon.com, and the cookie is Lax so the cross-site redirect carries it.
- **Cloudflare token:** the platform `CLOUDFLARE_DNS_API_TOKEN` is valid but sees only the nxeon.cloud zone, not trynxeon.com. I checked read-only and created nothing. The DNS script needs a token you create, scoped to trynxeon.com, or you add the record by hand. The script creates only the `workspace` A record, refuses if the host already exists, and defaults to a dry run.
- **DNS and cert:** create the record DNS-only first, issue the certificate with certbot HTTP-01 (as the other vhosts do), then flip it to proxied. While proxied, the origin accepts only Cloudflare IPs on 443 for this host.
- **Tests and checks:** `tsc` is clean and the 24 new tests pass. I also ran the nginx config on a private throwaway instance and the installer against stubbed tools. The production nginx was never touched.
- **Not verified:**
  - certificate issuance and renewal behind Cloudflare;
  - the node-4 firewall rule and the packet path to the VM;
  - the cross-site hop in a real browser;
  - the new routes under a real Next build.
- **Owner steps:** nine, starting with setting `WORKSPACE_UPSTREAM_SECRET` in `/opt/nxeon/.env` and promoting the branch. Runbook section 4 has the order, and section 6 has the rollback.
